Some people rarely or never get hangovers—often estimated at roughly 5% to 25% of drinkers depending on how hangover resistance is defined . Researchers point to a mix of genetics, biology, and drinking habits.⁠OMRF.org  +2[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESeAHEIkXXCS3K7Wqkqky_h0odp9hE3z0ijWhTdcID7UyLXCMSYQs_BhJZYMAlJmEZGwMovqX_WZmgUZOMDVtCuaoRXVM8tPtMm02YiZCO_AmkEWGn7ehu1LeWR3ZKn7IB1uh1XLRVwnJC5oy9BJQrOcCTpJZPRjx0WQ)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESmgEBxCJF12sZDmj4sou5DowsddZGV9old9nH6bNlp-lZv_eNw2X23ZI2BQ0AWuUwq7nK7F7eDV8Za0q8TLBKJ72zYRdtC8rwdXAl9wfkmC5NDXkSXXAq7GbMpOa24JkAlfV3lZuy2I-Yw7VThkmPzRC2o39wrPu4ucKbQAAHXg1_PAOOtvW7BaakVCSTZ0ha0bdrWM8ZXbkxtC1k)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESgwEBxCJF1y9Fz3TLwMzZRIyGpeAB7IumbMvadiz9c5xhLCxYWp3GcziDGNuAvadckV3CBFVyoFu04TI7wh9n_iSGKlYEgB5s9GfcAeXOUSIRZyyezLcRF2QrA6Gk__NM6mU0mrJ_JbWsjO5D0mLqd6wUepA_1An0LEHnuF1s7eBka2aUvA)

### Key Reasons You Might Not Get Hangovers

- **Genetics and alcohol metabolism:** Variations in liver enzymes (like ADH and ALDH) affect how quickly you break down alcohol and its toxic byproduct, acetaldehyde. Faster, cleaner processing can reduce lingering symptoms.⁠Columbia University  +2[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESmgEBxCJF12sZDmj4sou5DowsddZGV9old9nH6bNlp-lZv_eNw2X23ZI2BQ0AWuUwq7nK7F7eDV8Za0q8TLBKJ72zYRdtC8rwdXAl9wfkmC5NDXkSXXAq7GbMpOa24JkAlfV3lZuy2I-Yw7VThkmPzRC2o39wrPu4ucKbQAAHXg1_PAOOtvW7BaakVCSTZ0ha0bdrWM8ZXbkxtC1k)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESgwEBxCJF1y9Fz3TLwMzZRIyGpeAB7IumbMvadiz9c5xhLCxYWp3GcziDGNuAvadckV3CBFVyoFu04TI7wh9n_iSGKlYEgB5s9GfcAeXOUSIRZyyezLcRF2QrA6Gk__NM6mU0mrJ_JbWsjO5D0mLqd6wUepA_1An0LEHnuF1s7eBka2aUvA)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESwQEBxCJF17QuodxrjoGB7BkNyUHoFYhWZKzRdaT9mVF3H-Iiw29BEeAqhIy12CioQ1CaJgj0kUfLrtHykfQ2RxYd5ainyWfyEbW1fviUKff0fOQQ5yscUgX7F4VhXH93K4RbXw9hgVIq4yb9M-tB7mtonNgYit1kIo05KST5-jFJ2hFBUdAsh4xhEURc8Xk__SVzVQhY_zL5jh2OsppYHSzbnb3W_C6BjGAj5G39ls76rNZW-BaBXuCn81tCdGLg1k4J)
- **Lower inflammatory response:** Alcohol triggers inflammation that makes many people feel sick. People with a lower inflammatory response or stronger baseline immune balance may feel fewer hangover effects.⁠The New York Times  +2[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESgwEBxCJF1y9Fz3TLwMzZRIyGpeAB7IumbMvadiz9c5xhLCxYWp3GcziDGNuAvadckV3CBFVyoFu04TI7wh9n_iSGKlYEgB5s9GfcAeXOUSIRZyyezLcRF2QrA6Gk__NM6mU0mrJ_JbWsjO5D0mLqd6wUepA_1An0LEHnuF1s7eBka2aUvA)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbAHEIkXXuO0GSX86a8casT3JWN-D7XWWT07bxOKlWqljZWj_pt0cnyg5fzi0EdxSJTdwCmLW2PLCr5ZM0qTgDIhzD1dLxSyZdloyyBBeqAljCetpT-xrV4mHU0WkKZnATjftCAKIHypqC7VqEg)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESeAHEIkXXCS3K7Wqkqky_h0odp9hE3z0ijWhTdcID7UyLXCMSYQs_BhJZYMAlJmEZGwMovqX_WZmgUZOMDVtCuaoRXVM8tPtMm02YiZCO_AmkEWGn7ehu1LeWR3ZKn7IB1uh1XLRVwnJC5oy9BJQrOcCTpJZPRjx0WQ)

On [Reddit](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkQEBxCJF19te_YbJdzlezyaH2acknOj8PfjMMh3OjmOZh3j8P7zp6ZJd_09LvlghltSi36LBlIIiyAlU3fTaXSxizL9dZTUsmhQhGGV445H1hb5QFWviP1cC1A5-zmyv_TswjFdXvluDwEcs_cyqGBGLRyNs0U-hJuibKLB3PSdKT5YkxpxAkDHj2vHNjRRkSOhv) , opinions on metabolism's role are mixed, with some users pointing to fast metabolism as a reason they avoid hangovers while others debate how metabolism affects dehydration and timing.⁠OMRF.org  +1[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESeAHEIkXXCS3K7Wqkqky_h0odp9hE3z0ijWhTdcID7UyLXCMSYQs_BhJZYMAlJmEZGwMovqX_WZmgUZOMDVtCuaoRXVM8tPtMm02YiZCO_AmkEWGn7ehu1LeWR3ZKn7IB1uh1XLRVwnJC5oy9BJQrOcCTpJZPRjx0WQ)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkQEBxCJF19te_YbJdzlezyaH2acknOj8PfjMMh3OjmOZh3j8P7zp6ZJd_09LvlghltSi36LBlIIiyAlU3fTaXSxizL9dZTUsmhQhGGV445H1hb5QFWviP1cC1A5-zmyv_TswjFdXvluDwEcs_cyqGBGLRyNs0U-hJuibKLB3PSdKT5YkxpxAkDHj2vHNjRRkSOhv)To help put this in context, how **much and how often** do you usually drink, and do you tend to **eat or hydrate** when you do?

items.title: Key Reasons You Might Not Get Hangovers
items.text: Genetics and alcohol metabolism: Variations in liver enzymes (like ADH and ALDH) affect how quickly you break down alcohol and its toxic byproduct, acetaldehyde. Faster, cleaner processing can reduce lingering symptoms. Lower inflammatory response: Alcohol triggers inflammation that makes many people feel sick. People with a lower inflammatory response or stronger baseline immune balance may feel fewer hangover effects. Lower stress and anxiety: Hangover-resistant drinkers tend to report lower baseline stress and anxiety, which can influence how strongly your body reacts the next day. Drinking habits and drink choices: Eating food beforehand, pacing drinks, staying hydrated, getting decent sleep, and choosing drinks lower in congeners (like clear spirits over dark ones) all lower hangover odds. Tolerance or moderate intake: You may simply drink in moderation. However, not getting hangovers can also happen as alcohol tolerance builds with frequent, heavy drinking—sometimes masking symptoms or delaying when withdrawal/hangover effects show up.
